title: No coal, 90% water recycled: Inside Shahi exports' sustainability push
summary:
Shahi Exports is advancing sustainability through renewable energy, water recycling, coal elimination and greener production processes, while aligning with global brand climate targets. 
The company says true circularity goes beyond recycling to responsible sourcing and labour practices.  
However, adoption of sustainable products remains constrained by limited consumer willingness to pay a premium.

title: From boilers to balance sheets: LPG hike squeezes India’s textile hubs
summary:
India’s textile and apparel hubs are reeling from a steep increase in commercial LPG prices, sharply inflating production costs amid weak global demand and intense price competition.
From Surat to Tiruppur and Noida, manufacturers face pressure from rising fuel and labour costs, while limited pricing power, worker shortages and infrastructure challenges are also squeezing margins and operations.

title: Liquidations continue to outpace resolutions under IBC: Ind-Ra
summary:
India’s Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code recovery outcomes remain constrained by execution delays despite recent reforms, according to the Ind-Ra. 
In Q4 FY26, liquidation cases continued to outnumber resolutions, while recoveries stayed near 31 per cent of admitted claims. 
The agency said prolonged timelines, litigation delays, and NCLT capacity constraints continue to weigh on the insolvency process.

title: UK commits to 87% cut in climate emissions by 2040
summary:
The UK has set out its proposed level for the seventh Carbon Budget, which sets a target of close to 87 per cent emissions reduction between 2038 and 2042. 
This will protect family finances, grow the economy and tackle the climate crisis. 
Plans include cutting bills and costs; delivering energy security; generating jobs and attracting investment, and focussing on cleaner air and nature recovery.

title: Bangladesh cabinet approves FDI Incentive Scheme policy
summary:
The Bangladesh cabinet recently approved the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Incentive Scheme Policy, 2026.
The approval came at the cabinet’s ninth meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. 
The policy aims at encouraging expatriate Bangladeshis and other Bangladeshi citizens to contribute to attracting FDI through the government’s incentive support.

title: China to host 100 plus import promotion events globally in 2026
summary:
China’s Ministry of Commerce will organise more than 100 import promotion events in 2026 to help global companies expand exports to China.
The initiative, themed ‘Exports to China’, will begin with events in Belarus and Germany, including its first programme in the European Union, while promoting stronger international trade cooperation.

title: India meets FY26 fiscal deficit target; ICRA flags FY27 risks
summary:
India met its FY26 fiscal deficit target of 4.4 per cent of GDP, with the deficit contained at ₹15.2 trillion (~$159.7 billion) due to expenditure cuts and higher miscellaneous capital receipts, according to ICRA. 
However, the agency warned FY27 could see a 40-basis-point fiscal slippage amid West Asia conflict risks, rising subsidies and pressure on oil-related revenues and bond yields.

title: South India cotton yarn weakens as domestic, export demand slows
summary:
India’s cotton yarn market stayed subdued this week as weak domestic and export demand weighed on prices in Mumbai and Tiruppur.
Spinning mills cut yarn rates due to sluggish buying and limited export inquiries.
Meanwhile, Gujarat cotton prices remained steady despite the duty exemption, supported by stable arrivals, cautious purchases, and unchanged CCI auction rates.

title: Global acrylonitrile prices weaken amid feedstock and demand pressure
summary:
Global acrylonitrile (ACN) prices weakened across Asia, Europe and the US in late May and early June 2026 as buyers limited purchases amid soft ABS resin and textile demand.
Falling crude oil and propylene costs further pressured the market, while cautious buying and uncertain downstream recovery are expected to keep ACN prices under pressure in the near term.

title: US Upland cotton sales rise 21%; Pima rebounds sharply: USDA
summary:
US cotton export sales showed mixed trends in the week ended May 28.
Upland cotton net sales rose 21 per cent to 185,300 RB, led by Vietnam, Pakistan, Türkiye and China, though shipments fell 15 per cent.
Pima cotton sales rebounded 95 per cent to 5,400 RB, while exports reached a marketing-year high of 18,700 RB, driven by strong demand from India and Vietnam.

title: US’ Torrid Q1 FY26 sales fall 7.6% despite guidance beat
summary:
Torrid Holdings reported first-quarter FY26 net sales of $245.8 million, down 7.6 per cent year-on-year, while net income fell to $0.4 million from $5.9 million. 
Comparable sales declined 1.7 per cent and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $17.6 million. 
The company closed 20 stores during the quarter and expects FY26 net sales between $940 million and $960 million.

title: Bangladesh garment exports slip to $35.3 bn in July-May
summary:
Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports fell 3.41 per cent year-on-year to $35.31 billion during July 2025-May 2026, with knitwear exports down 4.26 per cent and woven garments down 2.42 per cent.
Home textile exports rose 3.48 per cent to $853.26 million, while cotton product exports declined 11.23 per cent.
RMG and home textiles accounted for 82.57 per cent of the country’s total exports.

title: EU deadstock ban 2026: Fashion’s unsold inventory reckoning
summary:
From July 2026, large companies in the EU can no longer routinely destroy unsold apparel, footwear and accessories, shifting fashion towards stricter inventory accountability.
Backed by ESPR rules and upcoming disclosure mandates, brands must now prove how deadstock is reused, repaired, donated or recycled.
The change pressures forecasting, returns, traceability and resale systems.

title: Canada’s Lululemon reports mixed Q1 results, lowers FY26 outlook
summary:
Lululemon has reported mixed Q1 FY26 results, with net revenue rising 4 per cent to $2.5 billion, driven by 22 per cent international growth, while Americas revenue declined 3 per cent. 
Gross margin fell 410 basis points to 54.2 per cent and diluted EPS dropped to $1.69. 
The company lowered its FY26 outlook, citing macroeconomic headwinds and softer demand in the Americas market.

title: US’ Caleres reports strong Q1 FY26 growth led by Brand Portfolio
summary:
Caleres has reported Q1 FY26 net sales of $666.6 million, up 8.5 per cent YoY, driven by 20.6 per cent growth in its Brand Portfolio business. 
Adjusted EPS rose to $0.38, exceeding guidance, while gross margin improved 200 basis points to 47.3 per cent. 
Famous Footwear sales declined 2.5 per cent. 
The company expects modest sales growth and improved profitability for full-year FY26.

title: Jordan’s apparel exports fall 21.7% in January-April 2026
summary:
Jordan’s apparel exports fell 21.7 per cent year on year to $695.3 million in January-April 2026, mainly due to a 25.3 per cent decline in shipments to the US, its largest market.
Despite the slowdown, the US accounted for over 71 per cent of exports.
Mexico emerged as the second-largest destination, with imports nearly doubling, indicating gradual diversification of Jordan’s export markets.

title: Indian T&A to get 5% tariff edge in Oman, SIMA hails trade pact
summary:
SIMA said the India-Oman CEPA will give Indian textile and garment exporters a 5 per cent tariff advantage, helping them compete more effectively and expand market share in Oman.
With duty-free access for most exports and Oman serving as a gateway to GCC region and East Africa, SIMA expects stronger growth in apparel and home textile exports from key textile hubs.

title: Sri Lanka’s garment exports fall 7.4% to $1.5 bn in Jan-April 2026
summary:
Sri Lanka’s garment exports declined 7.4 per cent year on year to $1.50 billion in January-April 2026, while textile exports fell 5.6 per cent, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka.
Combined textile and apparel exports totalled $1.62 billion, accounting for 45.7 per cent of industrial exports.
April textile and garment exports also weakened amid continued global demand uncertainty.

title: South Korea’s apparel imports rebound in April, reach $4.05 bn
summary:
South Korea’s apparel imports rose 1.15 per cent year on year to $4.05 billion in January-April 2026, supported by a 4.4 per cent increase in April that reversed recent weakness.
Knitwear imports outperformed woven garments, while exports of man-made filaments and knitted fabrics declined amid weaker global demand and growing competition from lower-cost textile-producing countries.

title: The invisible tariff: Compliance is now apparel’s toughest border
summary:
Tariffs are no longer the only trade barrier, as proof of origin, traceability, labour compliance and sustainability data increasingly determine market access.
EU DPP, EPR and parcel rules, alongside stricter US forced-labour scrutiny, are turning compliance into a competitive advantage.
Exporters able to scale trusted data systems may gain stronger buyer confidence and sourcing preference.
